subject: Archaeology
title: The Boy King: Tutankhamun's Short Life
description: Learn The Boy King: Tutankhamun's Short Life in one minute.

hook.text: Tutankhamun became pharaoh at 9 and died at 19. His fame comes from his death, not his reign.

buildup.text: He reversed Akhenaten's religious revolution, restoring Amun's temples and moving the capital back to Thebes.

discovery.text: CT scans reveal he had a broken leg, malaria, and a club foot. His health was terrible from inbreeding.

twist.text: His tomb was small and hastily prepared — likely meant for someone else and reassigned when he died young.

climax.text: DNA confirmed his parents were siblings. Genetic damage from royal inbreeding probably shortened his life.

punchline.text: The most famous pharaoh was a sickly teenager buried in someone else's tomb.

quiz.question: What did DNA analysis reveal about Tutankhamun's parents?
options: They were commoners who seized the throne
They were siblings, causing genetic damage from inbreeding
They were foreign rulers from Nubia

details.summary: Tutankhamun became pharaoh at age nine and died around age nineteen. His short reign reversed Akhenaten's religious revolution, restoring traditional Egyptian gods. Though a minor king historically, his intact tomb made him the most famous pharaoh in modern times.
details.whyItMatters: Tutankhamun's fame stems entirely from archaeology — his undisturbed tomb revealed what royal burials contained. Without Howard Carter's discovery, this minor pharaoh would remain a historical footnote.
takeaways: Tutankhamun ruled from age nine to about nineteen
He reversed Akhenaten's religious reforms to traditional gods
His intact tomb made him history's most famous pharaoh

faq.question: How did Tutankhamun die so young?
faq.answer: CT scans and DNA analysis suggest he had malaria, a bone disorder, and a broken leg that may have become infected. He likely suffered from genetic conditions due to royal inbreeding. No evidence supports murder theories that once dominated popular accounts.

faq.question: Why was Tutankhamun's tomb so important archaeologically?
faq.answer: It was the only virtually intact royal tomb found in the Valley of the Kings. Over 5,000 artifacts — gold mask, chariots, furniture, food — revealed the full richness of Egyptian royal burial that tomb robbers had destroyed in every other known royal tomb.
